avoid_hardcode.policy: Domain rules, thresholds, source authority, feature weights, phase policies, chip rules, finance rules, scoring constants, scheduler cadence, and performance budgets must be config/registry driven unless a literal is structurally intrinsic to the implementation.
avoid_hardcode.exceptions: Any unavoidable hardcoded value must be documented with rationale, owner, and test coverage.

modular_authority.policy: If a domain can reasonably be separated into a dedicated module or registry, V5 should do so by default whenever separation improves identification, adjustment, authority clarity, provenance, testing, maintenance, or reuse. Consumers must depend on the shared authority instead of duplicating logic.
modular_authority.performance_guard: Do not create runtime fragmentation that causes material latency regression. Prefer cached registries and stable module boundaries over repeated file reads, duplicated transforms, or excessive indirection.
modular_authority.discoverability: Every separated domain should be registered in config/v5_module_registry.json with its plane, entrypoint, controlling config, status, and adjustment surface.

performance_first.policy: Every material V5 change must be evaluated for correctness and processing speed. Prefer single-pass transforms, bounded candidate universes, cached immutable lookups, vectorized/batched operations where useful, and avoid repeated network or file reads.
performance_first.acceptance: Performance regression beyond configured budgets blocks promotion unless explicitly reviewed.
